lede: The biggest thing on the government calendar this week is the July 15 HARC meeting, where the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave goes before the commission for three separate preliminary large-scale public hearings covering multiple new buildings in an Accommodations 2 zone — the kind of project that shapes what Telluride looks like for a long time. The same day, the Board of County Commissioners takes up two Land Use Code amendments, including new rules for natural medicine businesses and nonconforming lots, while San Miguel County's sixth housing code working session on July 16 keeps pushing toward final recommendations on zoning, density, and workforce housing incentives.
